extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers and anyone seeking an overview of OpIndia, media watchers and those interested in disinformation and Indian political media
extracted.subtask_description: Identification of criteria and recurring practices used to evaluate the reliability, partisanship, and ethical practices of an online news website (here, OpIndia). Useful for assessing accuracy, bias, legal risks, and editorial standards of a news outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishes disinformation / fake news
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia is 'known for frequently publishing disinformation' and has published numerous fake news items and misreports (fact-checkers identified dozens of false or misreported stories between 2018–2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and counts: IFCN-certified fact-checkers identified 25 fake news stories and 14 misreported stories (Jan 2018–Jun 2020); Newslaundry and Alt News documented additional instances. Use third-party fact-check counts and documented corrections as measures of reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Islamophobic commentary and anti-Muslim content
rubrics_metrics.description: The site has frequently published Islamophobic commentary and content that portrays Muslims negatively, including repeated focus on Muslim actors and groups in COVID-19 and other coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies and content analyses (e.g., Discourse & Society, ACM conference paper) found a high proportion of Islamophobic framing: e.g., ~66% of top COVID-19 articles portrayed Islamophobic behaviour. Track topic and target frequency to evaluate bias and harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear partisan alignment (Hindutva / pro-BJP)
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia is openly right-leaning; it criticises 'liberal media' and supports the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Hindutva ideology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial statements and ownership/investor ties (links to Swarajya, Kaut Concepts, etc.) indicate partisanship. Partisan alignment should be measured by declared editorial positions, ownership, and systematic favourability in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrays mainstream media mistakes as 'fake news'
rubrics_metrics.description: A recurring pattern where OpIndia labels misquotes, incorrect headlines, or errors in mainstream outlets as 'fake news' and often persists with the claim even after corrections are issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the outlet distinguishes between errors and deliberate misinformation; check whether retractions/corrections by others change its coverage. This is an indication of a disinformation-enabling rhetorical tactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shaming and attacking journalists' integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia has a practice of attacking the 'professional integrity' of journalists it considers opposed to the BJP, alleging misconduct like sexual harassment, plagiarism, financial misconduct, or malicious editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether allegations are sourced, corroborated, or produced by monitoring journalists' social media for 'inconsistencies'; repeated unsubstantiated personal attacks indicate targeted harassment rather than accountability journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleging mainstream media partisanship or conspiracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The outlet frequently accuses mainstream media of being biased against the ruling party and of participating in a 'news media conspiracy' favourable to opposition actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for persistent claims of systemic bias without proportional evidence. Repeated conspiracy framing about other outlets is a signal of polemical rather than investigative coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplifying criticism and downplaying corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia amplifies celebrity or official criticism of mainstream outlets and often emphasises criticisms while minimising or downplaying subsequent corrections or apologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the outlet gives balanced coverage when targets correct errors; amplification without context can mislead readers about the scale and seriousness of alleged failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleging bias against India and Hindus
rubrics_metrics.description: The website frequently frames mainstream outlets as 'anti-India' or 'anti-Hindu', including charges that coverage favours minority groups or the opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor framing choices (language, headline emphasis). Patterns of accusing others of anti-national or anti-majority bias are indicators of identity-based partisan framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of in-group/out-group language and pronoun patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Content analyses found systematic linguistic patterns: first-person pronouns and positive descriptions for Hindus (in-group) and third-person pronouns and negative descriptions for Muslims (out-group), contributing to polarising discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative discourse analysis (pronoun usage, valence of descriptors) can be used as a metric of dehumanising or polarising rhetoric; such patterns indicate targeted identity framing rather than neutral reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of conspiracy theories and loaded labels
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia promotes narratives like the 'love jihad' conspiracy and uses charged labels ('Taliban', 'Al Qaeda', 'mob') to portray Muslims as violent offenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track recurrence of conspiracy themes and use of fear-invoking labels; presence indicates agenda-driven framing and potential for incitement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and copyright violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The site has been documented engaging in plagiarism and copyright violation, republishing others' material without attribution (e.g., coverage of Pulitzer-nominated photographers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check attribution practices and instances flagged by media-watchers (Alt News, Newslaundry). Plagiarism undermines credibility and editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doxxing / publishing personally identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia published real names and employers of Wikipedia editors it accused of being 'Islamists' or 'leftists', an act described as publishing personally identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing PII of private individuals tied to ideological criticisms is an ethical breach and risk factor (can lead to harassment). Such practices were central to its blacklisting on Wikipedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejected for IFCN fact‑checker certification (transparency & partisanship concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2019 the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN) rejected OpIndia's application to be certified as a fact checker, citing political partisanship, lack of transparency, and questionable fact‑checking methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet independent fact-checking standards (transparency about funding, corrections policy, methodology) is a concrete indicator of low fact‑checking reliability and limits marketplace credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blacklisted by Wikipedia / labelled 'unreliable source'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Wikipedia community declared OpIndia an unreliable source in March 2020, leading to its blacklisting for use as a reference on Wikipedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion on aggregator or encyclopedia blacklists (with documented reasons) is a signal used by researchers and editors to judge source reliability; document the reasons for blacklist decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal risks and FIRs related to reporting (incitement, obscenity)
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia faced first information reports (FIRs) and legal notices over specific reports (e.g., Bihar human sacrifice claims), including charges under the Information Technology Act and IPC section 295A (inciting religious outrage); some FIRs were stayed or quashed by courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track legal actions and their grounds (obscenity, incitement, doxxing); repeated legal exposure for content indicates potential for harmful or unlawful reporting practices and may reflect editorial recklessness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensationalized, identity-focused headlines and framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations found multiple articles with headlines explicitly naming Muslims as perpetrators and using sensational language to provoke communal sentiment (e.g., 28 articles naming Muslims as perpetrators within a short timeframe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline analysis (naming of community identities, sensational claims) can measure sensationalism and communal targeting. Frequent identity-centred headlines are a red flag for hate-inducing framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of reader contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia accepts article contributions from its readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open submission policies without transparent editorial oversight can increase risk of unverified or partisan content. Evaluate contributor vetting, editorial review, and correction policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization, advertising and external funding influence
rubrics_metrics.description: OpIndia's revenue mix includes advertising and donations; it received advertising and experienced advertiser withdrawals after 'Stop Funding Hate' campaigns, and claimed donation spikes when advertisers left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess funding sources, ad partnerships, and responses to funding-pressure campaigns; commercial incentives and sponsor relationships can shape editorial choices and vulnerability to deplatforming effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: External fact‑checking tallies as performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party fact-checkers (Alt News, Boom, Newslaundry) compiled tallies of false and misreported stories attributed to OpIndia (used as empirical measures of its accuracy record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aggregated fact-check records from independent organizations as a quantitative metric for accuracy over time; consider counts, severity, and whether corrections/retractions were issued.
